newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ciller, Turk president discuss anti-rebel actions.
newsitem.headline: Ciller, Turk president discuss anti-rebel actions.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller discussed the fight against Kurdish rebels with President Suleyman Demirel on Monday after newspaper reports linked her to a scandal involving anti-rebel gangs.

"The president and I...are sensitive on the subject of legitimate forces being used in all of the state's struggles. We are in total agreement on this subject," Ciller told reporters after meeting with Demirel.

The Yeni Yuzyil daily reported Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had received a report saying Ciller paid 250 billion Turkish lira ($8.3 million) from a slush fund to a Turkish underworld gang in 1994 to kill Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) head Abdullah Ocalan.
The head of the gang, Abdullah Catli, died last month in a crash in the same car as a senior police official, prompting speculation about links between state officials and far-right gangsters.

Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) has taken the brunt of criticism. One DYP deputy resigned as interior minister after the crash and another, Sedat Bucak, who was injured in the accident, was quizzed by a prosecutor last week.
The Yeni Yuzyil report said members of the Kurdish tribe headed by Bucak were involved in the plan to kill the PKK's Ocalan.
"Turkey has carried out every struggle with legitimate forces. To look for something outside of constitutional rule is misleading and wrong," Ciller said after seeing Demirel.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the PKK's 12-year-old armed struggle against the Turkish state for self-rule in the southeast of the country. ($1=30,000 TL average in 1994)
